motivo: Día centrado en el anuncio de Google sobre la IA y el buscador en cuentas escolares, con un debate largo en ChatGPT-IA-edu, y una actividad de Física compartida en Vibe Coding Educativo.

piezas.titular: Teachers debate Google’s announcement that switches off AI and search by default in school accounts
piezas.entradilla: Google has announced that Gemini and Google Search will be switched off in primary and secondary school student accounts until administrators turn them on. In the groups, the news sparked a discussion about who decides how AI is used in a school.
cuerpo: According to [Engadget](https://www.engadget.com/2305432/google-says-that-students-in-schools-that-ban-ai-wont-have-access-to-search/), which cites Chris Phillips, Google’s vice-president and general manager for education, the company announced on 3 November that access to Gemini, Gemini Notebook, Gemini in Classroom and Google Search will be switched off in primary and secondary (K-12) school accounts until administrators explicitly turn it on. Google clarified to the outlet that each product can be enabled separately and that it is not an all-or-nothing option. The new controls will roll out over the coming months.

The news reached the group first as an alarmist social-media version (“schools that ban AI will lose Google Search”). Members asked for it to be checked, and Engadget’s clarification was then shared. According to the same outlet, students at a school that blocks AI will not have access to Search and will see a message from their school saying so.

Several positions were put forward in the discussion. One welcomes AI being a decision for the school, and switching it off entirely if the school so chooses, for consistency with not allowing other AI chatbots. Another fears that access to information will be made conditional on accepting AI, and recalls that such access is a right. A third places digital coordinators between Google’s offer and caution about younger students, and awaits new guidance from the Catalan education department. Members also asked that teachers be able to monitor what students type, and argued for training teachers and families first, without rushing.

The Departament d’Educació’s guidance on the use of AI in schools was published in September 2026, and the newspaper [reviewed it in its Library section](pieza:2026-11-02/cat-orientacions-ia), although the project page on [XTEC](https://projectes.xtec.cat/ia/orientacions-per-lus-de-la-ia-en-educacio/) still describes it as “under development”.

fuentes.titulo: Engadget: Google says that students in schools that ban AI won't have access to Search
Orientacions per a l'ús de la IA en educació (XTEC) (in Catalan)

piezas.comprobado: Engadget (WebFetch, repasado): fecha 3-11-2026, autoría de Kris Holt, Chris Phillips como vicepresidente y director general de educación de Google, desactivado por defecto en cuentas K-12, habilitación por producto, mensaje del centro sin acceso a Search si se bloquea la IA, despliegue en los próximos meses. XTEC (WebFetch): documento «en desenvolupament», previsto septiembre-octubre del curso 2026-27; la página no menciona a menores de 14 años, por lo que se ha quitado esa referencia. No hay entrada original de Google localizada (WebSearch), la información se atribuye a Engadget. Mensaje de Telegram 53933 comprobado: es el que abre el tema. Las posturas son lo dicho en el grupo y no se han verificado.
piezas.ilustracion: Esquema de un interruptor general con cuatro palancas individuales (Gemini, Gemini Notebook, Gemini en Classroom, Búsqueda) que el centro puede activar o dejar apagadas una a una, frente a un único interruptor de todo o nada tachado.
piezas.ilustracion_alt: On the left, an all-or-nothing master switch crossed out with a red X; on the right, four individual switches (Gemini, Notebook, Classroom and Search), two switched on in blue and two off.
piezas.correccion: Corrected on 4 November 2026: an earlier version stated that the Generalitat’s guidance had not been published, as the XTEC page says; that page is out of date. Corrected on 13 November 2026: the standfirst said “AI-powered search” where the source refers to Google Search. Update on the same date: the official link from which the guidance was downloaded ceased to exist in early November, as reported in the group, and the XTEC page still describes it as “under development”.

piezas.titular: A gamified activity takes the gravitational field in Year 13 Physics to nine orbital missions
piezas.entradilla: “Misiones orbitales”, by El profe de la bata, asks students to create an astronaut and complete nine missions using interactive simulators. The practice version runs in the browser, with no accounts.
cuerpo: “[Misiones orbitales](https://elprofedelabata.github.io/misiones-orbitales/)” is a Physics activity for the second year of Spanish Bachillerato (Year 13) on the gravitational field, created by El profe de la bata. Students create their astronaut and complete nine missions; for each one they consult interactive simulators, from which they obtain the data needed to calculate orbital and escape velocities, apply Kepler’s laws, find orbital energy or deduce the mass of a star.

There are two versions. The practice version runs directly in the browser, with no accounts and unlimited attempts, although it is not intended for grading. The classroom version is installed with Google Apps Script, uses Google Workspace accounts, allows one attempt per mission, saves progress in a teacher’s spreadsheet and includes a dashboard for projecting. Scores are expressed in stars according to the error made: below 5% earns all of them.
The project is distributed under a CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 licence.

fuentes.titulo: Misiones orbitales, repository and guide (in Spanish)

piezas.comprobado: Repositorio de GitHub (WebFetch, repasado): descripción, nueve misiones, dos versiones, práctica sin cuentas e intentos ilimitados, versión de clase con Apps Script, hoja y panel, estrellas (error <5 % = todas), autoría y licencia CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. La demo carga (modo práctica, contador de 18 estrellas) pero no muestra autoría ni licencia. Se han quitado lo no confirmado en la fuente: nombres concretos de los simuladores, «tercera ley» de Kepler, «datos nuevos en cada intento», «mismo código y puntúan igual». Mensaje de Telegram 14590 comprobado.
piezas.ilustracion_alt: A planet surrounded by a blue elliptical orbit with nine dots, one per mission (“9 missions”), and on the right three stars earned with an error below 5% (“Error < 5%”).

piezas.titular: A Geography teacher uses Gemini to build a counter of births and deaths around the world
piezas.entradilla: “Pulso Demográfico Mundial en Tiempo Real”, by Ricardo Chao Prieto, simulates in real time the births and deaths in each country, based on the UN’s population projections for 2026.
cuerpo: Ricardo Chao Prieto, a teacher of Geography and History, has embedded the app in [a post on Geografiando](https://geografiaagustinos.blogspot.com/2013/10/cuanta-gente-nace-y-muere-al-dia-en-el.html), the Year 9 Geography blog of the Agustinos Fathers’ school in León, and shared it in the group as made with Gemini. It starts from an estimated world population of about 8.326 billion people and keeps adding births, at an average of about 4.2 per second, and deaths, about 2 per second.

These are not real records but a statistical simulation using each country’s rates, as the app itself states. It shows the net growth accumulated during the session, lets users filter by continent, speed up by five or twenty times and pause, and includes a map and a table by country with its population, birth rate and death rate. The blog post accompanies it with the daily figures and a chart on the fall in the global fertility rate. For the classroom, it makes visible figures that are hard to picture when written down.

fuentes.titulo: Geografiando: ¿Cuánta gente nace y muere al día en el mundo? (in Spanish)

piezas.comprobado: 04-11-2026, a mano: abierta la entrada del blog (vuelta a publicar el 3-11-2026, aunque la dirección conserva 2013/10) y la aplicación incrustada; cifras, controles y la nota de simulación, leídos en la propia aplicación. Juanjo probó que funciona. La había descartado la redacción por la fecha de la dirección.
piezas.ilustracion: Un globo terráqueo esquemático con dos contadores a los lados, uno de nacimientos (+) y otro de defunciones (−), y una flecha hacia arriba con el crecimiento neto
piezas.ilustracion_alt: A globe in the centre with a births counter on the left, marked with a blue plus, and a deaths counter on the right, with a minus, and a red arrow pointing up to indicate net growth.

breves.texto: In EduMedia-IAG, members explained how to use MotionVideo’s skills: you install the skill in the AI, invoke it and give it the instruction with the details of the video you want to create. Each example video on the site comes with its prompt, as the [piece of 3 November](pieza:2026-11-02/motionvideo-skills) reported.

In the United States, the Los Angeles school district [blocked students’ access](https://laist.com/brief/news/education/lausd-students-barred-artificial-intelligence-tools) to generative AI on their devices in September, and the FCC is [reviewing E-Rate subsidies](https://www.chalkbeat.org/2026/09/23/e-rate-school-internet-subsidies-threatened-in-screen-time-backlash/) for school internet connections amid the row over screen time. They were shared in the group as context for [Google’s announcement](pieza:2026-11-03/google-ia-cuentas-escolares).

descartado: Beca de residencia de Anthropic (EduMedia-IAG): fuera del tema del grupo, su propia moderación lo indicó y la fuente es un agregador no oficial.
Mensaje de OpenAI sobre pestañas Chat y Work y aviso de cambios de tokens en diciembre: sin fuente comprobable y comentario breve.
Informe del MIT, infografías en HTML/SVG, agentes de consola con datos del alumnado, motionvideo y cursor IA de Mollick: ya publicados el 2-11.
Anuncio del diario (nuevas secciones), /misrecursos y bot: administración interna.
Documento del MIT en la Biblioteca digital: tiene su propia sección.
repaso: Google: cargo de Chris Phillips precisado (vicepresidente y director general de educación) y «totalmente desactivado» pasa a «desactivado» (no es cita literal verificada).
Google: el aviso al alumnado se ajusta a Engadget (sin acceso a Search y mensaje del centro).
Google: quitada la referencia a las orientaciones que desaconsejan la IA a menores de 14 años y la de Google «para todas las edades», no confirmadas en fuentes.

Misiones orbitales: quitados simuladores concretos, «tercera ley de Kepler», «energía necesaria para cambiar de órbita», «datos nuevos en cada intento» y «mismo código y puntúan igual», que la fuente no recoge; añadido «intentos ilimitados» en la práctica.
Actualizado el campo comprobado en ambas piezas.
04-11-2026, a mano: corregido el último párrafo de google-ia-cuentas-escolares (la XTEC estaba desactualizada) y añadidos dos breves.
04-11-2026, a mano: añadida la pieza pulso-demografico, descartada por error por la fecha de su dirección.
